We also deeply appreciate the centrality of UNDP's governance and crisis work. However, a sound fundament alone is not enough. UNDP will also need to consider innovative ways to operationalize and implement the ambitions of the new Plan, whether through differentiated country engagement, shifts from implementation to capacity building, or more focus within the thematic mandates. We expect the new Plan to include different scenarios for various levels of funding. I would also like to stress the importance of UNDP's normative role. The Strategic Plan must showcase a human rights approach, including a focus on leaving no one behind, gender equality, and the SDGs. And this brings me to my second and last point. How UNDP positions itself in the multilateral development system is relevant also in the context UN 80 and the ongoing UNDS reform. To achieve the SDGs, we need a multilateral system built on complementarity, and we need a system that delivers as one at country level. We therefore see a strengthened role of the Resident Coordinator as crucial, and we kindly request UNDP to continue to operate in support of the RC system. We also expect We expect UNDP to outline more concretely its added value and how it will work together and in complementarity with other UN agencies. Good luck to you and thank you very much.
I thank the Netherlands. We will next hear from Brazil and then Japan. Brazil, please.

Thank you, President. Mr. President, Mr. Administrator, I'm very pleased to join myself and my delegation to the long and deserved list of appreciation to you and to your work. The Administrator's visionary leadership has been instrumental in strengthening UNDP's global impact, resilience, and credibility, even amidst a very complex development landscape. Under his stewardship, the Programme has not only adapted to global shocks, but also embraced structural transformation. We are grateful for its recent support to Brazil in its G20 presidency and as we prepare to host COP30 in Belém. These initiatives are a testament to UNDP's effectiveness, reliability, commitment to inclusive development, and alignment with national priorities. I also note the longstanding support provided by UNDP to our South-South cooperation initiatives. Mr. President, as we look to the future, Brazil is confident that the next Administrator will build on its legacy— on this legacy of excellence, which will be key to addressing the considerable challenges ahead. It must be operationally ready to help developing countries navigate the turbulent waters of diminished political commitment with and a steep decline in finance for development. In this context, The single most important task before us is to secure and strengthen the financial foundation of UNDP. The projected one-third reduction in core contributions by 2026 is alarming. Core funding is not just another budget line; it is the lifeblood of the Programme's capacity to operate independently, to innovate, and to deliver equitably across all Programme countries. We commend the efforts already underway to implement the Business Model Review, enhance operational efficiency, and anticipate austerity measures. However, these internal efforts must be matched by renewed political and financial commitments from traditional donors to preserve the integrity of UNDP's mandate and ensure continuity of support, especially for the most vulnerable. Development assistance must be seen as a long-term investment worth preserving, certainly to the benefit of recipients, but also of donors. Looking ahead, the discussions on the strategic plan for 2026-2029 will be pivotal. Brazil supports a bold and forward-looking vision aligned with the QCPR that reaffirms UNDP's role as a champion of sustainable development, a driver of structural transformation, and a catalyst for South-South cooperation. In closing, Brazil reiterates its support to UNDP, including the upcoming transition. And to you, Mr. Administrator, we do wish you all the best in your future endeavors. Thank you.
Thank you, Brazil. Next we have Japan, who will be followed by India. Japan, please.

Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to thank Administrator Steiner for your reflections on UNDP's achievements. Under your leadership. Japan applauds your significant contributions to transforming UNDP into an agency as strong and credible as it is, despite numerous challenges over the past 8 years. Looking ahead, Japan reaffirms its strategic partnership with UNDP. On that note, Japan made its second core contribution today, bringing this year's total above last year's. Japan welcomes the direction of the draft Strategic Plan for 2026 to 2029. The plan not only addresses key global challenges, but also builds on UNDP's core strengths. On crisis resilience, we fully support UNDP's vital role as bridge builder across humanitarian, development, and peacebuilding efforts, and its renewed commitment to conflict prevention early recovery, and peacebuilding. Turning to the emerging challenge of the declining official development assistance, ODA, UNDP has already taken important steps to address this trend. With its track record of prudent financial management, we believe UNDP will be able to achieve the right balance between improving its operational efficiency, and sustaining its field presence and operational capacities to deliver on its core mandate. We also support UNDP's continued efforts to diversify its funding base. Given the growing importance of mobilizing private sector funds, we welcome UNDP's role in catalyzing private sector partnerships. In this connection, private sector partnerships will be one of the main agenda of TICAD 9, which Japan is co-hosting in Yokohama in August, together with UN, UNDP, World Bank, and African Union Commission. And finally, your recognition of human development not as competing with national security but addressing insecurity's root causes resonates with us, as it is in line with the notion of human security. which both UNDP and Japan have long been advocating. And lastly, as Administrator Steinmeier's tenure draws to a close, Japan wishes to renew its gratitude for his resolute leadership in advancing UNDP's mandate and multilateral development cooperation. I thank you.
Thank you, Japan. India has the floor, please.

Thank you, India. We will next hear from the Permanent Representative of the Solomon Islands, who will be followed by Nigeria. The Solomon Islands, please.

UNDP has in the last 8 years carried out important interventions in the advancement of the Agenda for Sustainable Development, and we thank him immensely for the progress achieved. This hub aims to support startups in the financial services— I mean, financial services sector, contributing to Sustainable Development Goals and promoting innovation in in the financial sector. UNDP and Mastercard Foundation's Accelerator Lab programs has actively supported young SDG innovators in Nigeria to transform food system, promote climate resilience, and explore key trends which harness strategic innovation, digitalization, and development financing. An NGO named the Tony Elumelu Foundation run by a distinguished Nigerian, partners with UNDP for the Youth Connect program, which focuses on youth entrepreneurship and empowerment in Africa and plans to support 1,000 African entrepreneurs over 10 years. Thank you, Mr. President. I also thank the Administrator for his comprehensive statement. We would like to begin by commending UNDP for the tangible progress under the current Strategic Plan, notably in supporting the livelihoods in crisis, driving digital transformation, and enabling renewable energy access. As we look ahead to the next Strategic Plan, the entire UN development system faces critical challenges, including a decline in contributions and the multilateralism crisis. The ongoing UNAID initiative presents a rare opportunity to address these challenges. Against this backdrop, I'd like to highlight a few points. First, we encourage UNDP to pursue innovative reform measures under the UNDS cluster of the UNAID initiative in close consultation with the partners both within and beyond the cluster. As a co-lead of the UNDS cluster and integrator of the 2030 Agenda, UNDP should work closely with other agencies to shape a UNDS that is more streamlined, efficient, and result-oriented while ensuring that no one is left behind. Second, in line with the UNAID initiative, we encourage UNDP to undertake a comprehensive review of its current structure and functions. This review is particularly crucial given the anticipated decline in contributions. We recommend that UNDP, drawing on examples from sister agencies, consider relocating certain functions close to the field to enhance program delivery guided by the cost-effective analysis. Third, we welcome the inclusion of crisis resilience as a strategic objective in the draft Strategic Plan, an area where the UNDP holds a comparative advantage in advancing the HDP nexus. With the ongoing Humanitarian Reset discussions, including the simplification of the UN humanitarian cluster system, we would like to understand how this may affect UNDP's future crisis resilience efforts, in the next strategic plan. In closing, we thank Administrator Mr. Achim Steiner for your leadership over the past 8 years, which has brought meaningful progress across the work of the UNDP. We wish you continued success in your future endeavors. As demonstrated by our threefold increase in contributions to UNDP over the past 8 years, Korea will remain a steadfast partner in ensuring that No one is left behind. Thank you.

President, Administrator, dear colleagues, in the outset, I would like to express our deep appreciation to you, Administrator Herr Steiner, for your long service to the UN and the UNDP. Your unwavering commitments to development and poverty reduction has been a true inspiration to my country. Sweden welcomes the Secretary-General's UN80 initiative. Reform must be about protecting the fundamentals and adapting to new realities for a more efficient and effective UN. The reforms must focus on the UN's core mandates and make the best use of comparative advantages. This requires genuine coordination, firm prioritization, and committed action across the entire UN system. Sweden remains a staunch friend of the UN development system. Our contributions come with the highest expectations regarding effectiveness, transparency, and achieving clear and tangible results, not least at the country level. Sweden is among the few donors contributing a vast majority of the flexible funding to the UN development system, including to the UNDP. We must stress again that this situation is not sustainable. We encourage additional member states to step forward to meet their commitments in the UN Funding Compact. We welcome the draft strategic plan and appreciate a more focused approach with 4 strategic objectives instead of 6 signature solutions. However, we would appreciate clarification on how this will result in a sharper aim of your operations. Given the decrease in core funding, what specific changes can we expect in how UNDP operates and effectively delivers on the SDGs? The new strategic plan should also clarify that identifying gender equality as one of the 3 accelerators still means it will remain a central priority and a goal in itself. Finally, the plan should pave the way for full implementation of the UN Gender Equality Acceleration Plan. So with that, thank you very much, and allow me to wish you, Hakim, the best of luck in your future endeavors.
Thank you very much. Thank you, Sweden. Pakistan has the the floor, please.

Thank you very much, Mr. President. Allow me to begin by expressing Pakistan's profound gratitude to the Administrator, Mr. Achim Steiner, for his sterling leadership and able stewardship of UNDP over the past 8 years. We are proud of the partnership of UNDP with the government and people of Pakistan in advancing the SDGs, strengthening resilience, and achieving meaningful results, particularly for the most vulnerable. UNDP played a central role in supporting the response, under Mr. Steiner's leadership, including through its technical leadership in the post-disaster needs assessment and the co-development of the Resilient Recovery, Rehabilitation, and Reconstruction Framework. Appropriate focus must be provided to the eradication of poverty as the overarching goal. We encourage UNDP to continue prioritizing country-level presence, flexibility, and responsiveness. Finally, we take this opportunity to call on all partners to sustain and increase their financial support to UNDP. Predictable and flexible funding is essential to enable UNDP to deliver on its mandate, respond to emerging challenges, and maintain its universal presence. In closing, Mr. President, my delegation reiterates its sincere gratitude to Mr. Steiner and wish him all the very best. I thank you.
